name: Naturlehrpfad Alpbachtaler Seenland
beschreibung:
Overview
The Alpbachtal valley and the Kramsach lake plateau boast an exceptional network of didactic nature trails, medicinal herb gardens, and family exploration walks. Contrary to common misconceptions, no nature trail exists at high-alpine Lake Zireiner See (which is an arduous mountain trek involving over 1,300 vertical meters). Instead, several official themed trails showcase the valley's gentle cultural and natural landscapes: The 'Leichter Lernen Wanderweg' (Easy Learning Trail) at Lake Berglsteiner See in Kramsach blends forest pedagogy with brain-gym exercises across 12 kinesiology stations. In Reith im Alpbachtal, the barrier-free 'Hildegard von Bingen Trail' showcases herbal lore in Tyrol's premier Hildegard show garden, while 'Juppi Zauberwald' on the Reither Kogel enchants young adventurers with water features, treehouse villages, and scavenger hunts.

Route & Requirements
The regional themed trails feature manageable distances, gentle ascents, and family-tailored amenities:
1. Berglsteiner See – Leichter Lernen Trail (Kramsach): Starting from Reintalersee East parking lot, this 4.3-kilometer loop gains approximately 150 vertical meters on a wide gravel forest road leading up to Lake Berglsteiner See (713 m). Along the way, 12 interactive stations encourage fun coordination and concentration games. The main ascent path is passable with all-terrain strollers, whereas the immediate shoreline path is a rooty woodland trail requiring sturdy footwear.
2. Hildegard von Bingen Trail (Reith im Alpbachtal): A 3.0-kilometer, completely level circular route (approx. 20 vertical meters) that is 100 percent barrier-free and stroller-accessible. It passes through the 900 m² medicinal herb garden with barefoot reflexology paths, reaches the 'Blattform' panoramic viewing platform, and skirts Lake Reither See.
3. Juppi Zauberwald (Reith im Alpbachtal): A 2.5-kilometer stroller-friendly adventure circuit situated at the mountain terminal of the Reitherkogelbahn (1,200 m). Features play towers, water splash parks, and enchanted forest huts. Pure walking time is about 1 hour; planned stay with children is 2 to 3 hours.
4. Mühlbachweg (Alpbach): A 2.2-kilometer contemplative creek trail featuring open-air Kneipp wading pools, a historic waterwheel, and alpine herb beds.
All trails welcome families with children of all ages. Dogs on leashes are permitted (note swimming restrictions in Lake Berglsteiner See).

Getting There
Trailheads are easily reached via the Inntal motorway A12 (exit Kramsach) following regional roads to Lake Reintalersee East parking lot (€5 daily fee). The Reitherkogelbahn terminal in Reith provides complimentary summer parking. By public transit, regional bus lines 621 (Kramsach lakes) and 4074 (Brixlegg–Reith–Alpbach) connect smoothly from the Brixlegg train station.

Tips
Access to all nature trails, the Hildegard herb garden, and Juppi Zauberwald is completely free of charge. Guests holding the Alpbachtal Card (included from one overnight stay) enjoy complimentary cable car rides on the Reitherkogelbahn (closed on Wednesdays). On warm summer afternoons, bring swimwear for Lake Reintalersee or Lake Reither See. Lakeside dining is available at the 712er Lounge right on Lake Berglsteiner See.
